title: Ten-minute embedding onramp runbook and failures catalog
summary: A compact, operational quickstart for getting embeddings integrated with the Redwood SDK in under ten minutes. Focuses on minimal setup, telemetry probes to validate signal, and a short catalog of observed failure modes with immediate mitigations.
audience: SDK integrators, solutions engineers, developer advocates running quick demos or pilot integrations with embeddings.
prerequisites: 1) Redwood SDK dev token (local dev). 2) Python 3.10+ environment. 3) Small text corpus (.csv or .jsonl). 4) Access to sandbox project in Redwood Console. 5) Optional: basic familiarity with vector DBs (Pinecone/Weaviate).
quickstart_steps: (0) Prepare: clone lightweight example repo: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples.git && cd sdk-examples/embedding-minimal
(1) Install: python -m venv venv && source venv/bin/activate && pip install -r requirements.txt (package includes redwood-sdk v0.x, tqdm)
(2) Config: export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-test-XXX; confirm with python -c "import redwood; print(redwood.ping())" (expect 200 OK/nonce)
(3) Small run: python ingest.py --input sample-snippets.jsonl --model text-embed-adept-1 --batch-size 32 --index local (script shows token usage estimate before run)
(4) Verify vectors: python query.py --q "what is our cancellation policy" --topk 5; inspect returned ids + similarity scores; expect top1 >= 0.78 for near-duplicate example (local test)
(5) Add telemetry: enable TXN-level spans by setting REDWOOD_TRACE=1 in env and re-run ingest; check Console > Projects > telemetry for per-request latency and tokens-per-request distribution
(6) Smoke test: run a simulated user flow: pytest tests/test_embedding_flow.py::test_end_to_end --maxfail=1 (fast path covers ingest -> query -> delete)
(7) Clean up: python cleanup.py --index local or use Console to delete test index; revoke sandbox keys after demo
telemetry_checklist: Confirm per-request latency histogram is captured (p50,p95,p99) for embed calls
Token count distribution for batched embedding requests (mean, median, outliers)
Batch success ratio and retry counts (should be 0 retries for 99% of calls in sandbox)
KV/prefix cache hit rate (if using cached embeddings for repeated inputs)
Downstream store write latency (vector DB or local index) and write failures per minute
Model fallback events: track when requests fall back to a cheaper/smaller model variant
Cost signal: estimated tokens-per-embedding * calls-per-minute plotted against expected budget
failure_catalog: AuthErr: 401 from Redwood API when key misconfigured — quick fix: export correct key, rotate if leaked; note: key TTL in sandbox is 24h
BadPayload: 400 when a record contains non-UTF8 bytes — mitigation: normalize text before ingest (utf-8, replace control chars)
BatchTooLarge: 413 for overly large batch sizes or combined request body — mitigation: reduce batch-size to 16 or stream in chunks
VectorDBWriteTimeout: writes time out to external DB during heavy load — mitigation: increase write concurrency, add retry/backoff, or use local index for demos
SemanticDrift: low similarity scores on expected duplicates (embedding model mismatch) — mitigation: pin model version to text-embed-adept-1@2024-08 and rerun small repro prompt set

SilentDrop: ingestion appears successful but later queries return fewer vectors — cause often eventual-consistency in external index/table; mitigation: wait for index refresh or use synchronous write mode for demo
RateLimit: 429 when hitting rate throttle — mitigation: implement exponential backoff with Jitter, surface user-facing retry message in demo UI
rollback_and_mitigation: If model regression detected: rollback to previous pinned model version via Console rollout -> rollback shortcut (documented in linked PR)
If vector DB instability: switch ingestion to local ephemeral index and route queries to local copy until DB healthy
If cost spike: enable cheap-embedding fallback policy and throttle ingest job; notify billing owner
experiment_plan: Short A/B spike: compare text-embed-adept-1 vs text-embed-lite-1 on a 500-record prompt set. Metrics: average downstream R@5, median similarity for duplicates, tokens per embed, end-to-end query latency. Run both for 2 hours during off-peak. Save seed prompts, tag runs in Console, and capture telem snapshots for p50/p95. Hypothesis: lite reduces cost by ~3x with minor hit (<6%) in R@5 for short queries.
